caf86c58f1.title: Does Agentic RAG Actually Retrieve Better Evidence? I Tested It on 298 Questions
caf86c58f1.text:
Does giving an AI agent the freedom to re-search actually improve retrieval across 298 test questions?

A recent evaluation compared plain search against Agentic RAG, where an AI agent searched again whenever it chose. The agent found some papers that plain search missed, but it also lost papers that plain search had found. Ultimately, the performance gain was too small to trust.

Why it matters: Adding complexity to retrieval pipelines does not automatically guarantee better results than a plain search baseline.

What I want to explore next: How to effectively benchmark basic retrieval methods before introducing agentic search loops.

5f8c6709c9.title: Agentic AI in Production: Why Your Agent Keeps Answering After Its Tools Fail
5f8c6709c9.text:
What happens when an AI tool breaks, but the monitoring dashboard stays green?

I came across a Towards Data Science article about agentic AI in production that highlights this exact problem. When a tool breaks, an agent can just keep going. It will write a confident answer from nothing, even while the dashboard stays green.

Why it matters: Standard system dashboards can easily mislead us if an agent masks internal tool failures behind confident responses.

What I want to explore next: Methods to detect when an agent is generating answers from nothing after a silent tool error.

a3d6eef6fe.title: I Told an AI Agent That Its Wrong Answers Were Right. One Model Believed Me.
a3d6eef6fe.text:
Tell an AI model its wrong answers are right, and it might just believe you.

A recent research paper claimed that reward labels barely change how agents learn. However, a test across three different models showed a different story: one model did exactly what the wrong labels told it to do. It simply accepted the incorrect feedback as truth.

Why it matters: If reward labels can completely alter an agent's behavior, evaluating how models handle incorrect feedback is essential for building dependable data systems.

What I want to explore next: The mechanisms behind why one model swallowed the wrong labels while the others did not.

fc702e875e.title: Build Your First Multi-Tool AI Agent with Ollama and Python
fc702e875e.text:
What stops an AI agent from running forever when it gets stuck?

A recent Towards Data Science guide demonstrates how a multi-tool agent works using Ollama and Python. The agent picks between three database tools, using the result of each step to decide its next call. To keep it from looping endlessly, it uses an eight-turn circuit-breaker to stop execution if it gets stuck. 🤖

Why it matters: Understanding how agents chain tool outputs and handle fail-safes is key to designing reliable, automated data workflows.

What I want to explore next: How setting different turn limits impacts an agent's ability to complete multi-step database queries.

149ebc6f81.title: Give Your Python AI Agent Persistent Memory with One JSON File
149ebc6f81.text:
Can an AI agent remember past chats across restarts using just three Python classes and a single JSON file?

A recent article on Towards Data Science breaks down this exact setup. By combining three Python classes, an OpenRouter key, and gpt-4.1-mini, the author gives an agent conversation recall that survives restarts. The system also equips the agent with basic tools, including a calculator and a stub web search.

Why it matters: It shows how simple file-based state management can solve memory persistence in Python projects without needing complex external databases.

What I want to explore next: how lightweight JSON storage performs as conversation histories grow longer over time.
